source_notes.finding: There is no host bridge. The example's eval_fn turns every callable in the context into source text with inspect.getsource() and pastes it in front of the code, and every other variable as name = repr(value). Tools therefore run inside Pyodide, not on the host, and only if their source is self-contained: a tool that uses a module-level import (as math_example.py's sin uses math) fails with NameError (P1, P9). A self-contained copy returned 42 with 0 host calls (P1s).

Because tool source is copied into the sandbox, any secret a tool needs has to be inside the sandbox too (as a literal or via a permission the sandbox is given). Inferred from the eval_fn; nothing in the example keeps credentials on the host.
Upfront, the same create_default_prompt as the eval example: every tool's signature and docstring in the system prompt.

Deno's permission system around a Pyodide wasm runtime. Python's `js` module still reaches the Deno global (P12e printed Deno's version and pid), so the boundary that held was Deno's: file read, env and subprocess attempts all raised NotCapable (P12f, P5b, P12 os.system), and Pyodide's /etc/hosts is its own virtual file system (P4 Errno 44).

The example turns networking on (PyodideSandbox(allow_net=True), unrestricted). urllib cannot do https in Pyodide (P3), but js.fetch via pyodide.ffi.run_sync reached example.com with HTTP 200 (P3b). With allow_net=False the same call raised NotCapable (hardened-P3b).

timeout_seconds wraps process.communicate() in asyncio.wait_for and kills the Deno process (hardened P6 stopped at 30.0 s). memory_limit_mb only adds --v8-flags=--max-old-space-size, which does not bound Pyodide's WebAssembly memory: hardened P7 with 256 MB passed 4.1 GB and was killed by the harness.
A new Deno process per execution; variables persist only because the eval_fn re-injects them as repr() literals, so P8 printed 7. Values whose repr is not valid Python cannot carry over.
The generated wrapper catches every exception and returns {'error': str(e)}, so the model sees 'Error during execution: probe-boom' without the exception type or a line number (P10).

Median 1,135 ms per execution (P11): every call starts Deno, loads Pyodide and runs once. The in-sandbox P9 loop took about 975 ms more than an empty run (2,110 ms), so the five 200 ms calls ran serially.

langchain-sandbox 0.0.5, the version in langgraph-codeact's uv.lock, fetches its Deno entry point from a personal JSR scope at run time: PKG_NAME = 'jsr:@eyurtsev/pyodide-sandbox@0.0.3' (0.0.6 moved to jsr:@langchain/pyodide-sandbox@0.0.4). With node_modules_dir='auto', Deno installs npm packages next to the nearest package.json.

surprises: The Pyodide example is presented as the secure option, but it does not bridge tools to the host at all: it pastes each tool's source into the sandbox, which breaks any tool that relies on its module's imports, including the example's own sin/cos helpers that use math.
The example enables unrestricted network (allow_net=True) and sets no timeout, so the default run has network on and no time limit (P3b, P6).
memory_limit_mb does not limit Pyodide memory (hardened P7 reached 4.1 GB).

On first run Deno's node_modules_dir='auto' resolved to this repo's root package.json, installed every root dependency into the repo's node_modules/.deno, replaced six top-level node_modules entries and .bin with symlinks into it, and wrote deno.lock at the repo root. The versions match bun.lock and a bun import check still passed; deno.lock was removed, the node_modules layout was left as is. A deno.json in the probe folder now contains it.
